deliverables.text: Name the vent cap's 3D shape, state its face and edge counts.
Describe each layout's net (piece count/shapes); verify every weld seam edge is congruent.
Material cost comparison: sheets needed for 70 caps under each layout.
Labor cost comparison: total weld seams for 70 caps under each layout.
Total cost verdict: combine D3/D4, state margin, recommend.

balance.argument_a: Tighter nesting (14 caps/sheet vs 12) means fewer sheets bought -- real, disclosed material savings.
balance.argument_b: One fewer weld seam per cap, 70 times over, saves more in labor than A saves in material -- at a real, derived $3.00/seam production rate.
balance.margin_basis: Total job cost (sheets x price + seams x weld cost) for a 70-unit batch, computed in cases/vent-cap/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix C/D/E figures.

derived._note: Computed by cases/vent-cap/sensitivity_model.py, cost_breakdown(PARAMS). case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Derived from S5's real $26.28/hr direct-labor wage x ~6.85 min/seam for a small production tack/spot weld, not the S4 retail service-call price ($20-50), which includes shop overhead/minimum charge inappropriate for a repeated production weld.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5: margin ranges 4.80%-15.39%, Option B stays cheaper throughout.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Mara's own nesting-software output for this authored part; no public factory-nesting database exists. Grounded in the real fact that congruent triangles nest efficiently while composite folded shapes nest less efficiently.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not swept in Tier 2 probe 5 (authored part geometry, not a stated flex-eligible parameter).

modeling_assumptions.basis: Real, well-documented steel price swings of 30-50%+ over past tariff/demand cycles; not tied to a specific 2026 event.
